summary: An epitaxial 15.6 GHz AlN FBAR on SiC exhibits loaded $Q_	ext{max}$ increasing from 363 at 294 K to 1589 at 6.5 K ($Q f \approx 5.66$ to 24.79 THz), with acoustic performance limited by anchor loss at cryogenic temperatures and electrode resistance at room temperature. A temperature-dependent loss model incorporating Landau–Rumer and Akhiezer phonon scattering, thermoelastic damping, dielectric loss, and anchor radiation explains the measured $Q(T)$ trend and identifies the crossover near 270 K where $\omega_0\tau_\text{ph} = 1$.
motivation: High-frequency acoustic resonators above 10 GHz are needed for 6G filtering and cryogenic quantum-microwave circuits, but systematic characterization of epitaxial AlN FBARs from room temperature to mK remains scarce, leaving the dominant loss mechanisms at cryogenic temperatures unclear.
method: Small-signal RF reflection measurements ($S_{11}$) of a suspended 15.6 GHz AlN FBAR on SiC from 294 K to 6.5 K extract loaded Bode quality factors using group delay; a physics-based model with temperature-dependent AlN properties ($C_v$, $\kappa$, elastic constants, thermal expansion) decomposes losses from intrinsic phonon processes, thermoelastic damping, dielectric absorption, electrode resistance, and anchor radiation.
result: Anchor loss dominates at cryogenic temperatures (predicted $Q_\text{anchor}$ of order $10^4$), while electrode resistance limits $Q$ above $\sim$150 K; measured $Q$ remains $\sim10^2–10^3$ below the intrinsic Landau–Rumer limit, indicating room for improvement via better anchor isolation and lower-resistance (possibly superconducting) electrodes.
